- claim: `br update --claim --actor "<full agent name>"` sets assignee to the agent's full name in the export (verified in issues.jsonl); a second actor is refused (claim_exclusive).
- release: --status open --assignee "" clears the hold, keeps submitted/implemented.
- submitted: with transition comment "submitted: <branch>@<rev> -- <evidence>"; holder cleared; NOT ready afterwards (survives handoff). Without evidence or outside a stage, the gate FAILS submitted-without-evidence (observed before the stage existed — the rule fired correctly).
- implemented: coordinator transition with comment; gate OK implemented-without-evidence; a same-stage dependant of the implemented leaf becomes ready in .backlog/ready.mjs once the recorded revision is contained in the checkout (observed: lifemodel-ifm ready under stage lifemodel-hle).
- dependant claim where br refuses blocked claims: plain claim refused ("cannot claim blocked issue"), `--claim --force --actor ...` stays exclusive (second actor refused) and keeps the blocks edge.
- dependency cycle: br itself refuses the cycle at dep add ("Cycle detected"); check.mjs's cycle rules covered by its selftest fixtures.
- work record round-trip: runs.mjs claim printed a [shady2k-time v1] record; posted with `br comments add -f` unchanged; read back through the adapter byte-identical (cmp). Editing one number (35->34) in a copy makes the gate FAIL time-record-damaged.

- proof issues (lifemodel-lgu/ifm/hle and the cycle pair) closed/tombstoned afterwards; tracker back to its 4 real issues, gate green (new errors: 0).

- commit-msg (real hook): "no task link" refused; unknown task (lifemodel-zzzz) refused "task does not exist"; valid leaf (lifemodel-7ld) accepted. First setup commits made through the real hooks.
- pre-push (real hook, scratch remote /tmp): a tag on an existing commit passes "refs/tags/v1 introduces no commits: nothing to check"; a new branch on an existing commit passes likewise; a tag carrying a new unlinked commit (made with --no-verify to bypass commit-msg) is REFUSED (1 link problem, push failed rc=1); a push carrying a linked commit passes; a hook given no ref lines is refused ("an empty input is an error, never a pass", rc=1).
- connect in a fresh scratch clone: hooks active, unlinked commit refused, linked commit accepted; removing .backlog/rules/check-commits.mjs makes the next commit refused with "missing from this checkout; run npm run connect" (rc=1).
- present-documents on a scratch branch: moving docs/plugins/overview.md made the check report "new errors: 1" naming README.md: `docs/plugins/overview.md`; moving it back clean (new errors: 0).
- CI range calculations, run locally exactly as the workflow does: PR path (range merge-base..head, export at newest reachable) 2 commits checked 0 problems; push path (--introduced --before origin/main) 2 checked 0 problems; backlog-gate step against the merge-base baseline green (baseline empty at a pre-installation base — first-install case handled).

title: A new version replaces the running one without losing the conversation
description:
Charter: docs/charters/platform-1.md, outcome 1. Design: ADR-006 stage 1 (loader, immutable generations, blue/green cutover: standby, readiness, drain, lease handoff). The rollout is a loader command; who issues it (the owner, a deploy script, later the agent via core.generation) is not part of the outcome. Includes the one dialogue piece the charter keeps: stop/cutover finishes or requeues the cognition turn in flight instead of losing it.

## DONE WHEN
In the development test environment, a loader command brings up a new generation beside the running one; the measured switch gap is at most 2 s, and no Telegram update is lost or handled twice across the switch.

title: lifemodel runs on a test VM and rolls out, stops and panics on command
description:
Charter: docs/charters/self-change-1.md, outcome 4. The sandbox for an agent that changes its own code: a test VM, systemd, its own git checkout; roll-out = checkout + build + restart; panic = stop with a flag that keeps it down; a hard spending limit on the provider key.

## DONE WHEN
On the test VM one command rolls lifemodel out to a given commit and restarts it; panic stops it and it stays down across a VM reboot until resumed; the provider key carries a hard limit.

title: A panic command stops everything and nothing comes back until the owner resumes
description:
